title: Gysin purity calculus on regular affine schemes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. Let $u:U\to V$ be a compactifiable finite-type morphism between regular affine Noetherian excellent schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. A regular closed immersion means a closed immersion whose ideal is locally generated by a finite sequence, each member acting injectively on the quotient by its predecessors. Such a morphism is locally a regular closed immersion followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; its virtual relative dimension $e$ is the smooth dimension minus the codimension of the immersion, locally on components. If $V$ is the spectrum of a field $F$ and $U$ is integral, then $e=\operatorname{trdeg}_F\kappa(\eta_U)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree, def-weil-residue-field], where $\eta_U$ is the generic point. Use the ordinary etale $u^!$ right adjoint and signed Tate twists [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-per-potential-dualizing]. The Kummer-normalized fundamental class is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Cl}_u:\Lambda_U(e)[2e]\xrightarrow{\sim}u^!\Lambda_V.$$
For a regular immersion it is the absolute-purity Gysin class, and for a smooth morphism it is $\gamma_{u,\Lambda}$ of [lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation]. It is independent of a local factorization, commutes with etale localization and open restriction, and, for composable such morphisms $u:U\to V$ and $v:V\to W$, writing $e_v$ for the virtual relative dimension of $v$, satisfies
$$\operatorname{Cl}_{vu}=u^!(\operatorname{Cl}_v)\circ\operatorname{Cl}_u(e_v)[2e_v]$$
under the right-adjoint transitivity and Tate identifications. The analogous class for a localization of a regular scheme is obtained by restriction and has the same compatibility. These classes commute with regular (flat with geometrically regular fibres) change of base wherever the corresponding regular immersions occur. If $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is a finite purely inseparable field extension (in characteristic $p>0$, every element of $L$ has a $p$-power in $F$; in characteristic zero $L=F$), its virtual dimension is zero and, under the canonical etale equivalence $u^!\Lambda_F\cong\Lambda_L$, its class is multiplication by $[L:F]$.

source.place: Expose XVI, Theorem 2.3.2 (regular-immersion composition), Theorems 2.5.5 and 2.5.12 (factorization independence and composition), Theorem 3.1.1 and Corollary 3.1.2 (absolute purity); Expose XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.3 proof (purely inseparable degree) and Lemma 4.3.1.2 (regular base change). Smooth normalization uses the diagonal/DNC input lem-per-ordinary-smooth-orientation, not a trace construction
